corrections.claimed_speedup: SMHasher3 (AVX2 build of NMHASH): 25.44 GiB/s vs 13.02 GiB/s for XXH-64 and 15.52 GiB/s for CityHash-64 in the 262144-byte bulk test (raw/NMHASH.txt, raw/XXH-64.txt, raw/CityHash-64.txt). That is ~95% faster than xxHash64 and ~64% faster than CityHash64. rurban/smhasher shows a much smaller gap: nmhash32 at 12676.08 MiB/s and nmhash32x at 13072.64 MiB/s vs 11176.72 MiB/s for xxHash64, ~13-17% (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the published results, which were generated with SMHasher3 20251015/20251112/20260827 releases. The README's 'gcc 9.3' refers only to its older runtime-comparison section (SMHasher3 beta1).
corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 3950X, boost disabled, pinned to 3500 MHz (SMHasher3 README Performance section). Raw result files report speeds '@ 3.5 ghz'.
corrections.caveats: The 25.44 GiB/s figure is NMHASH32 ('nmhash32 v2' [avx2]); NMHASH32X ('nmhash32x v2') measured 25.50 GiB/s. Both are 32-bit-output hashes (there is no NMHASH64), so the xxHash64 comparison crosses output widths. The ~95% margin is an AVX2-vectorized NMHASH against scalar XXH-64. In rurban/smhasher the win shrinks to ~13-17%, and in the same SMHasher3 run NMHASH trails XXH3-64 (42.21 GiB/s) and roughly ties wyhash (23.17 GiB/s). SMHasher3 marks NMHASH as FAIL (172/250 tests passed) and NMHASHX as FAIL (150/250), against XXH-64 at 241/250. The hash-garage README claims both pass rurban/smhasher and demerphq/smhasher. Compile flags are unstated, which caps the tier at B.
